case.summary: Verdict: fraud at probability 0.90. Customer C13171 denied the $55.68 charge (3558054, 2016-12-19 22:08:56, online, product C), and the episode is a tight three-transaction cluster on the same generic device and hotmail.com email within 22 minutes — 3557979 ($55.60), 3557987 ($55.69, New device), and 3558054 ($55.68) — for total exposure $166.97, matching the card_not_present_new_device pattern. The decisive evidence is the customer denial (family: customer) plus the case-memory scorer's 0.9573 on the flagged transaction against a real-time risk_score of only 0.38, reinforced by 18 prior CLOSED confirmed-fraud cases on this same card with the identical pattern, most recently CC-5010, CC-4485, CC-4163, CC-3928, and CC-2716 (family: memory); against this, amount-within-baseline and a previously-seen device offered only weak legitimacy signal and did not satisfy the R7 recurring-charge gate (gap_cv 1.11 exceeds the 0.6 threshold). No evidence request was made — none was needed, and none would have moved a card with this dense a fraud history off a fraud verdict. The bank should create a case and block the card via the L1 route (exposure $166.97 ≤ $2,500); an analyst could alternatively read the $55.68 price point as a recurring hotmail.com charge given 7 same-amount prior purchases, but the irregular cadence (gap_cv 1.11) and the very high memory score argue against that reading.
